005package org.wpilib.util;
006
007import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
008
009/** WPIUtil JNI. */
010public class WPIUtilJNI extends WPIUtilJNIWrapper {
011  /** Checks if the MSVC runtime is valid. Throws a runtime exception if not. */
012  public static native void checkMsvcRuntime();
013
014  /**
015   * Write the given string to stderr.
016   *
017   * @param str String to write.
018   */
019  public static native void writeStderr(String str);
020
021  /**
022   * Enable mock time. The mock time is initially set to 0. This also sets program start time to 0.
023   */
024  public static native void enableMockTime();
025
026  /** Disable mock time. */
027  public static native void disableMockTime();
028
029  /**
030   * Set mock time.
031   *
032   * @param time The desired time in nanoseconds.
033   */
034  public static native void setMockTime(long time);
035
036  /**
037   * Returns the time.
038   *
039   * @return The time.
040   */
041  public static native long now();
042
043  /**
044   * Returns the timestamp at which the program started.
045   *
046   * @return The program start timestamp in nanoseconds.
047   */
048  public static native long getProgramStartTime();
049
050  /**
051   * Returns the system time.
052   *
053   * @return The system time.
054   */
055  public static native long getSystemTime();
056
057  static native int createAlert(String group, String id, String text, int level);
058
059  static native void destroyAlert(int alertHandle);
060
061  static native void setAlertActive(int alertHandle, boolean active);
062
063  static native boolean isAlertActive(int alertHandle);
064
065  static native void setAlertText(int alertHandle, String text);
066
067  static native String getAlertText(int alertHandle);
068
069  /**
070   * Creates an event. Events have binary state (signaled or not signaled) and may be either
071   * automatically reset or manually reset. Automatic-reset events go to non-signaled state when a
072   * WaitForObject is woken up by the event; manual-reset events require ResetEvent() to be called
073   * to set the event to non-signaled state; if ResetEvent() is not called, any waiter on that event
074   * will immediately wake when called.
075   *
076   * @param manualReset true for manual reset, false for automatic reset
077   * @param initialState true to make the event initially in signaled state
078   * @return Event handle
079   */
080  public static native int makeEvent(boolean manualReset, boolean initialState);
081
082  /**
083   * Destroys an event. Destruction wakes up any waiters.
084   *
085   * @param eventHandle event handle
086   */
087  public static native void destroyEvent(int eventHandle);
088
089  /**
090   * Sets an event to signaled state.
091   *
092   * @param eventHandle event handle
093   */
094  public static native void setEvent(int eventHandle);
095
096  /**
097   * Sets an event to non-signaled state.
098   *
099   * @param eventHandle event handle
100   */
101  public static native void resetEvent(int eventHandle);
102
103  /**
104   * Creates a semaphore. Semaphores keep an internal counter. Releasing the semaphore increases the
105   * count. A semaphore with a non-zero count is considered signaled. When a waiter wakes up it
106   * atomically decrements the count by 1. This is generally useful in a single-supplier,
107   * multiple-consumer scenario.
108   *
109   * @param initialCount initial value for the semaphore's internal counter
110   * @param maximumCount maximum value for the semaphore's internal counter
111   * @return Semaphore handle
112   */
113  public static native int makeSemaphore(int initialCount, int maximumCount);
114
115  /**
116   * Destroys a semaphore. Destruction wakes up any waiters.
117   *
118   * @param semHandle semaphore handle
119   */
120  public static native void destroySemaphore(int semHandle);
121
122  /**
123   * Releases N counts of a semaphore.
124   *
125   * @param semHandle semaphore handle
126   * @param releaseCount amount to add to semaphore's internal counter; must be positive
127   * @return True on successful release, false on failure (e.g. release count would exceed maximum
128   *     value, or handle invalid)
129   */
130  public static native boolean releaseSemaphore(int semHandle, int releaseCount);
131
132  static native long allocateRawFrame();
133
134  static native void freeRawFrame(long frame);
135
136  static native long getRawFrameDataPtr(long frame);
137
138  static native void setRawFrameData(
139      long frame, ByteBuffer data, int size, int width, int height, int stride, int pixelFormat);
140
141  static native void setRawFrameInfo(
142      long frame, int size, int width, int height, int stride, int pixelFormat);
143
144  static native void setRawFrameTime(long frame, long timestamp, int timeSource);
145
146  /**
147   * Waits for a handle to be signaled.
148   *
149   * @param handle handle to wait on
150   * @throws InterruptedException on failure (e.g. object was destroyed)
151   */
152  public static native void waitForObject(int handle) throws InterruptedException;
153
154  /**
155   * Waits for a handle to be signaled, with timeout.
156   *
157   * @param handle handle to wait on
158   * @param timeout timeout in seconds
159   * @return True if timeout reached without handle being signaled
160   * @throws InterruptedException on failure (e.g. object was destroyed)
161   */
162  public static native boolean waitForObjectTimeout(int handle, double timeout)
163      throws InterruptedException;
164
165  /**
166   * Waits for one or more handles to be signaled.
167   *
168   * <p>Invalid handles are treated as signaled; the returned array will have the handle error bit
169   * set for any invalid handles.
170   *
171   * @param handles array of handles to wait on
172   * @return array of signaled handles
173   * @throws InterruptedException on failure (e.g. no objects were signaled)
174   */
175  public static native int[] waitForObjects(int[] handles) throws InterruptedException;
176
177  /**
178   * Waits for one or more handles to be signaled, with timeout.
179   *
180   * <p>Invalid handles are treated as signaled; the returned array will have the handle error bit
181   * set for any invalid handles.
182   *
183   * @param handles array of handles to wait on
184   * @param timeout timeout in seconds
185   * @return array of signaled handles; empty if timeout reached without any handle being signaled
186   * @throws InterruptedException on failure (e.g. no objects were signaled and no timeout)
187   */
188  public static native int[] waitForObjectsTimeout(int[] handles, double timeout)
189      throws InterruptedException;
190
191  /** Utility class. */
192  private WPIUtilJNI() {}
193}
